title: The System of Rock-Cut Tunnels Near Gihon in Jerusalem Reconsidered
author: Ronny Reich; Eli Shukron
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted peer-reviewed journal article. Project stores its own summary of the argument only; no reproduction of plans, sections, or the article's text.
summary: Reich and Shukron's reassessment of the Gihon-spring rock-cut water-system complex (the Rock-Cut Pool, the Round Chamber, Channels II/III, and the Warren's Shaft system) in light of their own City of David excavations. Building on questions first raised by Yigal Shiloh's 1978-1985 excavations, Reich and Shukron argue that the natural karstic shaft later called Warren's Shaft was not originally part of a deliberately engineered water-access route usable from inside the city in David's period: the stepped tunnel that today leads to the top of the shaft only reached that point when the floor of an earlier Middle Bronze Age tunnel was cut down, apparently accidentally exposing the shaft, in the Iron Age II period (the era of the divided monarchy), centuries after the setting of 2 Samuel 5. This project cites this article as the named, checkable archaeological basis for the disclosure that the traditional identification of 2 Samuel 5:8's tsinnor with the Warren's Shaft system has been challenged on archaeological grounds — not as adopting any specific alternative identification of tsinnor, and not as taking a position on whether the shaft (as a natural karstic feature) itself may still be considerably older; the point at issue is whether it was a usable route into the city at the time of David's conquest, which this article's argument answers negatively.
